dedupe_keys.name: protect bio protection forest against rockfall on the fuorn pass road engadin

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the first practical use of the Swiss Protect Bio method, which lets hazard protection projects count the effect of forests and other biological measures, on an 800-metre stretch of the Fuorn Pass road near Zernez in the Engadin, Switzerland. Rockfall risk was described from past events, event maps and geological scenarios, and a model on a three-dimensional terrain model simulated rockfall tracks and the forces of different boulder sizes, with slope gradient, stem density and other forest factors included. Results showed that no rockfall nets are needed on about half of the stretch, where existing forest protects against events of 1 to 30 year return periods; nets are needed only where forest is thin, and felled trees laid across the slope are a low-cost complement. The method has since been applied at Gruobenwald, Klosters, Orvin, Täsch and Schmitten. The cost section notes that about half of Swiss forest is protection forest, maintained with about 145 million euros a year, against an estimated value of 3.8 billion euros a year. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal. Caveats: forest protection against avalanches, landslides and debris flows is hard to quantify, and data are not available everywhere. It illustrates simulation-based appraisal of nature-based landslide and rockfall hazard reduction for road infrastructure and climate adaptation; related records are the Dynamic World land cover data and the Hansen Global Forest Change data.
name: Protect Bio, protection forest against rockfall on the Fuorn Pass road (Engadin)
organisations: Canton of Grisons Office for Forests and Natural Hazards
outcomes: About half of the 800 m road stretch needs no rockfall nets because the existing protection forest suffices, saving the cost of technical structures.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from the Protect Bio project
